name: Crucible Loyalty Tattoo Overlay
description:
A semi-permanent dermal overlay — not ink, but a thin biocompatible film applied to the skin — displaying Crucible Genomics' loyalty insignia. The overlay changes in complexity with employee tenure: simple geometric patterns at five years, intricate circuit-like designs at ten, and a full sleeve of interlocking forge symbols at twenty. The overlay fades if not renewed annually at a Crucible facility.

The overlay is technically optional. In practice, employees who don't display loyalty markings find their advancement opportunities quietly limited. The annual renewal requirement ensures that former employees lose their markings — Crucible's way of saying you belong to them, or you don't.
functionality: Tenure display, loyalty signaling, corporate identity
what_it_says: You belong to Crucible and your skin says how long they've owned you.
story_hooks: A person with a twenty-year Crucible loyalty overlay is found dead in a the Gray Zone district — but Crucible's records show they were terminated fifteen years ago, meaning someone has been renewing their overlay outside official channels.

physical_description.visual_profile: A luminescent biofilm overlay that sits flush against skin, creating a second dermis layer of shifting geometric and circuit-pattern designs. The markings glow faintly under certain light conditions with a cool blue-green bioluminescence. On the wearer, it reads as both biological and technological — a hybrid claim of ownership branded directly onto the body.
physical_description.fit: Applied directly to skin surface; conforms perfectly to body contours. Typically covers forearm, wrist, or full sleeve depending on tenure. The overlay has negligible tactile profile — smooth, almost imperceptible to touch.
physical_description.primary_material: Biocompatible dermal polymer film — a synthetic skin layer engineered to integrate with natural epidermis without rejection. Self-adhesive, micro-porous.
physical_description.texture: Silky, nearly frictionless surface. Under magnification, reveals microscopic circuitry embedded within the translucent film. Slightly cooler to the touch than surrounding skin due to embedded thermoelectric elements powering the bioluminescence.
physical_description.color_scheme: Translucent base with embedded geometric patterns in deep indigo and cyan. The designs glow softly in dim light — circuit traces, hexagons, and interlocking forge-anvil symbols in phosphorescent blue-green. Over time, older overlays develop a faint amber undertone where the polymer begins degrading.
physical_description.closures: Permanent adhesion; requires enzymatic solvent at Crucible facility to remove. Annual renewal involves gentle abrasion and reapplication of fresh biofilm.
distinctive_features: Bioluminescent circuitry that pulses subtly with wearer's heart rate
Pattern complexity increases visibly with tenure — five-year simple geometry, ten-year circuit intricacy, twenty-year full sleeve
Fades to dull gray if not renewed within 14 months of application
Crucible Genomics forge-anvil logo always anchors the primary design
Thin enough to be invisible at distance but unmistakable up close
Micro-sensors track renewal compliance and report to Crucible HR systems
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 corporate badge. Wearing it signals mid-to-senior Crucible employee status; not wearing it signals either junior rank or deliberate defiance.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by Crucible Genomics employees as proof of loyalty and corporate integration. Wearing one marks you as company property in a literal sense. The social pressure to renew annually is enormous — not renewing publicly signals you're leaving or being forced out. Among the working class and sub-grade populations, it's a mark of corporate servitude and loss of bodily autonomy.
physical_description.condition_typical: Fresh overlays appear pristine and vivid. As they age toward renewal, the bioluminescence dims slightly and the patterns may develop hairline cracks. Heavily worn overlays (near end-of-life) appear dull gray with barely visible designs.
